chunks: And it was said to al-Sadiq عليه السلام: “Why do you say that a man’s mawla is from him?” He said:
“Because he was created from his clay, then they were separated, and captivity brought him back to him. So he showed compassion for what of him was in him, and freed him; therefore he is from him.”

key_terms.السَّبْيُ: captivity that led to the person being brought back
key_terms.طِينِهِ: his clay; indicating an original shared source or substance
key_terms.فَأَعْتَقَهُ: he set him free through manumission
key_terms.فَعَطَفَ: he showed compassion and tender regard
key_terms.مَوْلَى: a freed slave or client bound by allegiance to the man connected to him

ai.seo_question: Why is a freed slave considered to be from the man who frees him in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains why a freed slave is described as being ‘from’ the man who frees him. The Imam عليه السلام grounds this relationship in a shared origin, subsequent separation, and reunion through captivity, followed by mercy and manumission.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3495 - It was said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as): "Why do you say that a man's mawla (freed slave) is considered to be from him?"

Imam (as) said: "Because he was created from his clay, then they were separated, and captivity brought him back to him. So, he showed compassion for what was in him (the shared origin) and freed him. Therefore, he is considered to be from him."
